# Produced by, on the 144 GB container:
#   llama-eval-callback -m DeepSeek-V4-Flash-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00005.gguf \
#     -p "The capital of France is" --no-repack -c 512 -t 12
#
# Tokenizes to 5 ids, no BOS: 671, 6102, 294, 8760, 344.
#
# Format: name|op|shape|sum
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS ALONGSIDE THE ONE-TOKEN ORACLE
#
# v4flash-layer0-oracle.txt was captured at a single token, position 0. RoPE at
# position 0 is the identity, so in that trace q_pe has exactly the same sum as
# its input and *every* RoPE implementation passes -- including one that does
# nothing at all. That made the decoupled rotation unverifiable, and it is one
# of the five things this architecture makes easy to get wrong.
#
# Here positions run 0..4 and the rotation is real:
#
#   q_norm-0 (view)   {64, 64, 5}    695.835632   -> q_pe-0    4082.126465
#   kv_norm-0 (view)  {64, 1, 5}      24.049295   -> kv_pe-0     76.641815
#   attn_raw (view)   {64, 64, 5}   3432.786621   -> ROPE_BACK   28.466785
#
# Layer 0 has dsv4_compress_ratios[0] == 0, so it takes the plain RoPE path:
# freq_base 10000, freq_scale 1.0, ext_factor 0, attn_factor 1.0, betas 0,
# n_ctx_orig 0, mode NORM (deepseek4 maps to LLAMA_ROPE_TYPE_NORM, not NEOX).
# The YaRN parameters in the container apply to the *other* 41 layers.
#
# The sum is every element added together: a cheap and unforgiving checksum. A
# transposed matrix, an unrotated RoPE or a missing norm all change it, and none
# of them raise an error.
#
# Two notes on rows below:
#   * q_norm-0 is an RMS_NORM with no MUL after it -- that norm carries no
#     weight, unlike every other norm in the model.
#   * ffn_moe_probs-0 is SOFTPLUS then SQRT. That is what expert_gating_func 4
#     means; it is neither softmax nor sigmoid.
#
# This capture covers all of layer 0, through the MoE and the shared expert, and
# ends where layer 1 begins.
